This meager initial mass places the species among the more fecund cichlids, where large numbers of diminutive offspring compensate for limited per-offspring investment. The ultimate adult size presents a stark contrast: individuals can reach a maximum total length of 28.0 centimeters [Li = 28.0 centimeters] under favorable conditions, corresponding to an ultimate wet weight of approximately 300 grams [Wwi = approximately 300 grams] in large, well-nourished specimens. This dramatic growth trajectory, spanning over five orders of magnitude from hatching to adulthood, is characteristic of many mouthbrooding cichlids and underscores the species’ capacity for rapid structural development once exogenous feeding begins. Field surveys and laboratory rearing programs have consistently documented this size range, confirming that the species attains a substantial body mass relative to other tilapiine fishes inhabiting West African coastal lagoons.

Gonadal recrudescence proceeds rapidly once the length threshold is surpassed, allowing individuals to participate in the next available spawning event.

The ecological context of these life-history traits is best understood within the dynamic lagoon systems that Blackchin tilapia inhabits across its native range. The diminutive hatchling mass necessitates a rapid transition to exogenous feeding, as yolk reserves are exhausted within a few days post-eclosion. The modest adult size relative to the largest tilapias, such as Oreochromis niloticus, is compensated for by early maturity and high fecundity. The sustained reproductive output over several years allows populations to recover quickly from environmental perturbations such as seasonal salinity spikes or drought-induced habitat contraction. These demographic attributes position S. melanotheron as a classic r-selected strategist within the cichlid family, trading maximal somatic size for early and prolific breeding in variable coastal waters.
